result.scope_note: Verified that RFC 9110 (June 2022) specifies HEAD responses MUST NOT include a message body; the response to a HEAD request shall be identical to what a GET request would return, but without the body content.

explanation.text: RFC 9110 (June 2022 HTTP Semantics) states a server must not send a message body in a HEAD response — only headers, supported by spans 7 and 10.
RFC 9112 span 90 explicitly states a HEAD response ends at the empty line with no body, no matter what the fields say.
The worldwide HTTP standard published June 2022 consists of RFC 9110, RFC 9111, RFC 9112, as documented in spans 16, 32-36.

assessment.rationale: Spans 16, 32-36 establish that the worldwide HTTP standard was published in June 2022 as RFC 9110, RFC 9111 and RFC 9112, replacing earlier RFC 7230-7235. Span 32-36 show the published dates and document structure.
assessment.provenance_note: Spans 16-36 collectively document the June 2022 publication of the HTTP standard.

excerpts.text: * HTTP/1.1 is now specified across three documents published in June 2022: RFC 9110 "HTTP Semantics" (STD 97), RFC 9111 "HTTP Caching" (STD 98) and RFC 9112 "HTTP/1.1" (STD 99). RFC 9110 obsoletes RFC 2818 and RFC 7230 to 7235 (except 7234), RFC 9111 obsoletes RFC 7234, and RFC 9112 obsoletes the message syntax parts of RFC 7230.

| RFC 9110 | HTTP Semantics | 97 | June 2022 | RFC 2818, 7230, 7231, 7232, 7233, 7235, 7538, 7615, 7694; updates RFC 3864 |
| RFC 9111 | HTTP Caching | 98 | June 2022 | RFC 7234 |
| RFC 9112 | HTTP/1.1 | 99 | June 2022 | Portions of RFC 7230 |
